full_judgment:
8. Mr. Abdur Rob Chowdhury, Senior Advocate, appearing on behalf of the leave petitioner, submits that the Administrative Appellate Tribunal erroneously dismissed the Appeal Case No. 206 of 2003 on ground of limitation under the amended provision of the second proviso to section 4(2) of that Administrative Tribunal Act, 1980. The impugned order was made on 03.04.1996. The Departmental appeal was filed on 01.07.1996 and the authority rejected the appeal on 15.07.1998. Thereafter, the petitioner filed the A.T. Case No. 51 of 2002 on 11.08.1998. In the meantime, second proviso to section 4(2) of the Administrative Tribunal Act was amended on 19th November 1997. As the petitioner's case was pending long before the 19th November 1997, the bar to filing A.T. Case within two months from the date of service appeal would not be applicable to the petitioner. The amended provision did not have retrospective effect. By dismissing the appeal on ground of limitation, justice was denied to the petitioner. He further submits that having dismissed the appeal on the ground of limitation, the Administrative Appellate Tribunal did not go into the merit of the case and that the petitioner's case on merit was that the punishing authority had decided to withhold two annual increments but the Appellate authority enhanced the punishment to compulsory retirement which was not justified. He lastly submits that the ultimate punishment of compulsory retirement was harsh, excessive and disproportionate to the alleged offence and that secondly another employee who was similarly situated with the petitioner was given the punishment of withholding two annual increments and as such the petitioner was discriminated against. 

 I. Whether the learned Administrative Appellate Tribunal erroneously dismissed the Appeal Case No. 206 of 2003 on ground of limitation under the amended provision of the second proviso to section  4(2) of the Administrative Tribunal Act, 1980 and impugned order having been made on 03.04.1996 and the Departmental appeal having been filed on 01.07.1996 and the authority having rejected the appeal on 15.07.1998 and the petitioner having filed the A.T. Case No. 51 of 2002 on 11.08.1998 and in the meantime, second proviso to section 4(2) of the A.T. Act having been amended on 19th November 1997 and the petitioner's  case having been pending long before the 19th November 1997, the bar to filing A.T. Case within two months of the date of service appeal would not be applicable to the petitioner and the amended provision did not have retrospective effect and by dismissing the appeal on ground of limitation, justice was denied to the petitioner. 

 II. Whether the Administrative Appellate Tribunal having dismissed the Appeal on the ground of limitation did not go into the merit of the case and the petitioner's case on merit was that the punishing authority enhanced the punishment to compulsory retirement which was not justified.
